about.title: Costa Mesa Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a death in Costa Mesa is someone else's fault, the family is left holding two things at once: grief and a stack of practical questions no one wants to answer. California law gives certain relatives a way to seek accountability through a civil wrongful death claim. That claim belongs first to a surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children; where none exist, it can pass to other dependents or heirs. It is entirely separate from any criminal charges the Orange County District Attorney may pursue. Public records for 2025 show 619 injury collisions in Costa Mesa, 847 people hurt and 4 lives lost, with the heaviest reporting along Newport Boulevard, Harbor Boulevard and both directions of SR-55. Not every wrongful death begins on a roadway. Falls, medical errors, unsafe products and workplace incidents can also give rise to a claim. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Costa Mesa families with an independent wrongful death attorney who works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What Costa Mesa Families Should Know Before Filing

items.title: Only certain relatives can bring the claim
items.desc: California limits who has standing: the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by specific dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out who in your family is eligible so no one is left out or filing improperly.

items.title: The clock is shorter than most people expect
items.desc: Families generally have two years from the date of death to file, and far less time when a city, county or state agency is involved. Starting early protects your right to be heard.

items.title: Recoverable losses go beyond the funeral bill
items.desc: A wrongful death claim can seek funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. These are civil remedies, pursued separately from any criminal case.

items.question: My family member was killed in a crash on SR-55 in Costa Mesa. Does a criminal case replace a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: No. A criminal prosecution is brought by the state and decides guilt or punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action your family controls and that seeks compensation for your losses. The two can proceed at the same time, and a civil claim can succeed even when no criminal charges are filed. An attorney can review the collision report and insurance details specific to your case.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Standing goes first to the surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the decedent's children. If there are none, the right can pass to other dependents or heirs under the state's intestate rules. Because the order matters and families are often complicated, it helps to have an attorney confirm who should be named.

items.question: How long do we have, and what if a government vehicle or public road defect was involved?
items.answer: In most cases you have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit in California. When a government entity is a potential defendant, a separate administrative claim usually must be presented much sooner, often within six months. Missing that earlier step can close the door on part of the claim, which is why early guidance matters.
